All cell cultures were spun down to remove cells. 10mL of cell-treated lignin samples were acidified with HCl (final concentration of 1% (v/v)) and spun down (4000xg) to precipate the acid-soluble lignin. The supernatants were removed and washed several times and spun down. The final precipiate is then dissolved in 1mL of DMSO.
centrifugation to pellet cells and collect supernatant

Eucalyptus kraft lignin was dissolved in 100% DMSO, then resuspended in M9 growth media and filter-sterilized using a 0.22um bottle-top filter. The final concentration of the lignin represents 0.15%(w/v) of the M9 media. Fosmid clones were inoculated with the lignin-amended M9 media containing 1x mixed metals for enzymes requiring metal cofactors, as well as chloramphenicol (25ug/uL), and arabinose (100ug/uL) to maintain the fosmid and copy number within the EPI300 host strain.

Fosmid clones were inoculated with the lignin-amended M9 media containing 1x mixed metals for enzymes requiring metal cofactors, as well as chloramphenicol (25ug/uL), and arabinose (100ug/uL) to maintain the fosmid and copy number within the EPI300 host strain.

All cell cultures were spun down to remove cells. 1mL of cell-treated lignin samples were acidified with HCl (final concentration of 1% (v/v)) and spun down (4000xg) to precipate the acid-soluble lignin. The supernatants were removed and extacted with 3x volume of ethyl acetate and dried by N2 gas. During the ethyl acetate extraction process, I also spiked in with 100uM 3-chlorobenzoic acid as an internal standard to normalize the extraction process.
centrifugation to pellet cells and collect supernatant

Eucalyptus kraft lignin was dissolved in 100% DMSO, then resuspended in M9 growth media and filter-sterilized using a 0.22um bottle-top filter. The final concentration of the lignin represents 0.15%(w/v) of the M9 media. Fosmid clones were inoculated with the lignin-amended M9 media containing 1x mixed metals for enzymes requiring metal cofactors, as well as chloramphenicol (25ug/uL), and arabinose (100ug/uL) to maintain the fosmid and copy number within the EPI300 host strain.
EPI300 host harboring fosmid with environmental genes from pulp & paper bioreactor

The final concentration of the lignin represents 0.15%(w/v) of the M9 media. Fosmid clones were inoculated with the lignin-amended M9 media containing 1x mixed metals for enzymes requiring metal cofactors, as well as chloramphenicol (25ug/uL), and arabinose (100ug/uL) to maintain the fosmid and copy number within the EPI300 host strain.

During the ethyl acetate extraction process, I also spiked in with 100uM 3-chlorobenzoic acid as an internal standard to normalize the extraction process.
centrifugation to pellet cells and collect supernatant

Eucalyptus organosolv lignin was dissolved in 100% DMSO, then resuspended in M9 growth media and filter-sterilized using a 0.22um bottle-top filter. The final concentration of the lignin represents 0.15%(w/v) of the M9 media. Fosmid clones were inoculated with the lignin-amended M9 media containing 1x mixed metals for enzymes requiring metal cofactors, as well as chloramphenicol (25ug/uL), and arabinose (100ug/uL) to maintain the fosmid and copy number within the EPI300 host strain.

100mL cultures were set-up in 180mL sterile containers. At the time of sampling samples, 1% of cellulase was added to the culture. Incubated for 2 hours at 30C, with vortexing every 30 minutes. Undigested cellulose was collected using sterile forceps. Media was centrifuged (2 batches of 50mL of media, 10,000g x 20 min) and the pellets pulled together. The pellets were washed 2x with 1x PBS and placed at -80C until freeze drying.
Cultures were centrifuged (100mL), the pellet was resuspended 1X PBS, and centrifuged, PBS removed and repeated (2x washing). The pellet was retained, frozen and then lypholized
Collected in sterile 50mL falcon tube, later transferred to sterile Low-Bind tube

S 1 to S4 were ground in a 20 mL steal canister chilled in liquid nitrogen. After grinding, material was transferred to a 50 mL chilled canoical tube with a chilled spoon. S5 to S7 were ground in a 50 ml chilled canister. S8 was first crushed in a chilld mortar and pestil then transferred to a chilled 50 mL canister. Grinding was sufficient to obtain a uniform powder. For S1 to S4, grinding was for 45 seconds; for S5 to 6, 90 seconds; and for S7 and S8, 120 seconds.

Samples consist of segments of internode 4 (top internode) of the AP13 genotype of switchgrass at Elongation 4 (E4) stage. 35 Internode 4s per replicate (Between Node 3 and Node 4, counting up from the soil) were harvested  when at a length of  11-12.5 cm. Each biological replicate consists of segments of 35 internodes collected from > 5 individual clones between 1 pm and 1:30 pm during the specified date ranges. Leaf sheathes were removed and internode segments  immediately cut with a sharp blade and transfered to a tube submerged in liquid nitrogen, and then stored at -80°C.

Collected gels were washed with a series of buffers to remove media, remove bacteria cells and prevent microbial growth. Upon collection they were put in a buffer of  0.02% w/v sodium azide in 0.1M NaOH (24h) and placed on a shaking incubator (RT), followed by two washes (24 h) with 0.02% w/v sodium azide. After the third washing the gels were transferred to 0.01% w/v sodium azide (RT).
Cells were collected using sterile forceps (not vortexed), tranferred to a sterile container and carried through a series of washing as described in column U.

All cell cultures were spun down to remove cells. 1mL of cell-treated lignin samples were acidified with HCl (final concentration of 1% (v/v)) and spun down (4000xg) to precipate the acid-soluble lignin. The supernatants were removed and extacted with 3x volume of ethyl acetate and dried by N2 gas. During the ethyl acetate extraction process, I also spiked in with 100uM 3-chlorobenzoic acid as an internal standard to normalize the extraction process.

Eucalyptus kraft lignin was dissolved in 100% DMSO, then resuspended in M9 growth media and filter-sterilized using a 0.22um bottle-top filter. The final concentration of the lignin represents 0.15%(w/v) of the M9 media. Fosmid clones were inoculated with the lignin-amended M9 media containing 1x mixed metals for enzymes requiring metal cofactors, as well as chloramphenicol (25ug/uL), and arabinose (100ug/uL) to maintain the fosmid and copy number within the EPI300 host strain.

attribute.label: Seed culture preparation and inoculation details

properties.raw_value: To start each experiment with fungal suspensions in an equivalent metabolic state, seed cultures were prepared as follows. An agar square (0.5 cm2) with fungal mycelia was taken from agar plates maintained at 4°C, deposited on a fresh YMPG-agar plate (mycelia in contact with the agar), and incubated for 7 days at 28°C. Then, 4-5 agar squares (~0.5 cm2) with mycelia from the fungal mat edges were inoculated in non-baffled 250 mL flasks containing 50 mL of YMPG (pre-seed cultures) and incubated at 200 rpm and 28°C for 7 days. Resulting fungal pellets were homogenized (10 s, speed 6) in sterile conditions using an Omni Mixer 115V with a 50 mL SS Chamber PTFE (Omni International, GA, USA). The fungal suspension (2 mL) was re-inoculated in YMPG under the same conditions than the pre-seed culture for 5 days (to generate the seed cultures). Fungal pellets were homogenized as described previously and a ratio of 1:12.5 (v:v) of fungal suspension per media volume was used to inoculate the corresponding cultivations.

•	Cellobiose 5 g/L
•	Vanillic acid or Syringic acid 2 mM- in the corresponding cultivations (see experimental factor details)
•	Ammonium tartrate 2 g/L
•	MgSO4 0.5 g/L
•	KH2PO4 1 g/L
•	KCl 0.5 g/L
•	Trace elements: 1 mL (in 1 L):
o	Na2B4O7·H2O 0.1 g
o	ZnSO4 0.07
o	CuSO4·5 H2O 0.01
o	MnSO4·4 H2O 0.01
o	FeSO4·7 H2O 0.05
o	(NH4)6MoO2·4 H2O 0.01
•	Vitamins (ATCC Vitamin Supplement, https://www.atcc.org/Products/All/MD-VS.aspx) 1 mL/L
•	Alpha-tocopherol (antioxidant) 1 mM
•	Ascorbic acid (antioxidant) 5 mM

attribute.label: Seed culture preparation and inoculation details

properties.raw_value: To start each experiment with fungal suspensions in an equivalent metabolic state, seed cultures were prepared as follows. An agar square (0.5 cm2) with fungal mycelia was taken from agar plates maintained at 4°C, deposited on a fresh YMPG-agar plate (mycelia in contact with the agar), and incubated for 7 days at 28°C. Then, 4-5 agar squares (~0.5 cm2) with mycelia from the fungal mat edges were inoculated in non-baffled 250 mL flasks containing 50 mL of YMPG (pre-seed cultures) and incubated at 200 rpm and 28°C for 7 days. Resulting fungal pellets were homogenized (10 s, speed 6) in sterile conditions using an Omni Mixer 115V with a 50 mL SS Chamber PTFE (Omni International, GA, USA). The fungal suspension (2 mL) was re-inoculated in YMPG under the same conditions than the pre-seed culture for 5 days (to generate the seed cultures). Fungal pellets were homogenized as described previously and a ratio of 1:12.5 (v:v) of fungal suspension per media volume was used to inoculate the corresponding cultivations.

•	Cellobiose 5 g/L
•	Vanillic acid or Syringic acid 2 mM- in the corresponding cultivations (see experimental factor details)
•	Ammonium tartrate 2 g/L
•	MgSO4 0.5 g/L
•	KH2PO4 1 g/L
•	KCl 0.5 g/L
•	Trace elements: 1 mL (in 1 L):
o	Na2B4O7·H2O 0.1 g
o	ZnSO4 0.07
o	CuSO4·5 H2O 0.01
o	MnSO4·4 H2O 0.01
o	FeSO4·7 H2O 0.05
o	(NH4)6MoO2·4 H2O 0.01
•	Vitamins (ATCC Vitamin Supplement, https://www.atcc.org/Products/All/MD-VS.aspx) 1 mL/L
•	Alpha-tocopherol (antioxidant) 1 mM
•	Ascorbic acid (antioxidant) 5 mM

attribute.label: Other experimental details_flask/bioreactor size_volume media_feeding mode

properties.raw_value: Cultivations were conducted in 250 mL flasks containing 25 mL of media with cellobiose (5 g/L). Cultivations containing additional aromatic compounds (4HBA, vanillate or syringate) were prepared as follows. 2 mM aromatic compound was added in I. lacteus and P. ostreatus cultivations at 3 days respectively. After 24 h, another 2 mM aromatic compound was again supplemented. Samples for -omics were collected 6 h after the second feeding as well as the samples containing only cellobiose and corresponding controls. Every sample  contains antioxidants (5 mM ascorbic acid and 1 mM α-tocopherol), which were added in the media 30 min before the first aromatics feeding.
